transcript: So you know those really soft cookies that you get at the grocery store that taste really chemically but are also strangely addictive? We're going to be making them today, but a little bit better. Welcome back to Elevated Nostalgia, a series where I share my favorite childhood treats with the gourmet twist. Today we're recreating lofthouse cookies. It took some testing, but I finally landed on a recipe that recreates their impossibly soft and cakey texture without being overly sweet. We'll start off by whipping the butter and sugar until super light and fluffy. Then we'll add in the egg, egg white, and some almond extract to emulate that store-bought flavor. The secret to getting these cookies exactly like the ones at the store is in the dry ingredients. For this recipe, you'll need a bleached cake flour like swans down since it has a lower protein content that creates a soft and fillowy texture. After the dough is all mixed together, it needs to chill for an hour before scooping the cookies onto a tray. We'll bake them for around 12 minutes, but don't overdo it. When the cookies are done, they should be just barely golden brown on the edges and set on top, which will help them stay soft. Once they've had a chance to cool completely, I topped each of the cookies with a layer of buttercream frosting and some sprinkles then they're ready to enjoy. Of all the recipes I've recreated for this series, this is probably the one I'm most proud of. These copycats hit all the right notes of nostalgia with a velvety soft crumb, an identical loctahouse texture, and a classic sugar cookie taste that's a hundred times better than the original. To make them yourself, grab the full recipe on the blog with all my tips and tricks. But I'll see you next week for a second to last episode.
